{{nihongo|'''Afuchi Shrine'''|安布知神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, in {{ill|368|Q48000|qid=Q48000}} (56th year of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}}), an eight-petaled mirror was enshrined at Kiyozaka as the sacred proxy of {{ill|Omoikane|Q586088|qid=Q586088|lt=Yagokoro-Omoikane-no-Mikoto}}, and the shrine was founded under the name “Wadō Daijingū.”<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|author=|title=History of Achi Village|date=1984|year=|accessdate=|publisher=Published by the Achi Village History Editorial Committee|author2=|author3=|author4=|author5=|author6=|author7=|author8=|author9=}}</ref>
It has long had a close relationship with {{ill|Achi Shrine (Achi Village)|ja|阿智神社 (阿智村)|qid=Q11657447|lt=Achi Shrine}}, an {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki-listed shrine}} located several kilometers away. The shrine site is situated on a slope overlooking fields believed to be the site of the ancient {{ill|Tōsandō|Q1334011|qid=Q1334011}} “Achi Station.” In {{ill|706|Q23506|qid=Q23506}} (3rd year of {{ill|Keiun|Q428753|qid=Q428753}}), {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined together<ref name=":0" />. There was a period when it was known as “Yosaka Hachiman.”

In {{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}} (1st year of {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}}), the local lord of the {{ill|Ogasawara clan|Q2975340|qid=Q2975340}} enshrined {{ill|Shinra Myōjin|Q22127349|qid=Q22127349}} (Susanoo-no-Mikoto) from {{ill|Mii-dera|Q1756307|qid=Q1756307|lt=Mii-dera}} in {{ill|Ōmi Province|Q843882|qid=Q843882}}, and the shrine was renamed Silla Myōjin Shrine.<ref name=":0" /> {{ill|Tokugawa Iemitsu|Q314481|qid=Q314481}} donated a vermilion-seal land grant of 10 koku under the name Silla Myōjin, and thereafter renewed vermilion-seal documents were issued with each change of shogun.<ref name=":0" /> The current shrine buildings were reconstructed in {{ill|1671|Q7610|qid=Q7610}} (11th year of {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}}) by the ruling Miyazaki clan.<ref name=":0" /> The main hall is enclosed within a protective structure and is built in the sangensha nagare-zukuri style. === Shrine grounds ===
* Ancient holly tree: Designated a natural monument of Achi Village in 1968. Estimated age at the time of designation: 250 years.
* Ancient sakaki tree: Designated a natural monument of Achi Village in 1968. Estimated age at the time of designation: 100 years.
* Komainu (guardian lion-dogs): On both sides of the stone steps
* War memorial monument
* Temizuya (purification pavilion)
